rows.R: Table 2 p.6: door-to-balloon time has two adjusted contrasts, 6.18 min (-4.78 to 17.14) under 'Difference, %' and beta 13.00 (3.64-22.36); door-to-needle 0.40 vs 5.00. Footnote b describes both as marginal-effect differences; estimands undefined and inference discordant.
rows.evidence: jama_huffman_2018_oi_170166.pdf p.6 Table 2 rows, footnotes a-c; p.3 Statistical Analysis. Text layer; table structure checked against text order.
rows.rationale: For door-to-balloon time (STEMI) the table prints a 'Difference, % (95% CI)' of 6.18 (-4.78 to 17.14) and a beta-coefficient of 13.00 (3.64 to 22.36), both labelled adjusted for clustering and temporal trends through footnote b, which says these are differences in marginal effects from mixed-effects logistic or quantile regression. The two estimates of the same intervention-control contrast in minutes differ by a factor of about 2 and disagree on whether the CI excludes zero; the unadjusted median difference is 77-65 = 12 min. For door-to-needle the pair is 0.40 (-5.23 to 6.03) vs 5.00 (-5.20 to 15.20). The 'Difference' column is labelled as % for a time outcome. Neither the footnotes nor Methods define what each column estimates (marginal mean vs median quantile coefficient, scale, population). Legitimate distinct estimands could explain the numbers, so I do not call it confirmed, but as printed a reader cannot tell which adjusted effect applies, and the choice changes the inference for door-to-balloon time. Hence probable_issue, substantive, direct.

rows.R: Supp3 index p.1 names eFigure 1A 'Residual ... (Expected - Observed)'; caption on p.24 (rendered) says left/negative = MACE lower than mean, right/positive = higher. Under E-O, positive residual means lower than expected. Sign conventions conflict.
rows.evidence: joi170166supp3_prod.pdf p.1 index; p.24 eFigure 1A rendered at 130 dpi and viewed (axis -3 to 2, ranked hospitals, caption); main pdf p.9 narrative.
rows.rationale: With r = expected - observed, a hospital with observed MACE above expected has r < 0. The caption states the opposite mapping (left, negative = lower MACE than the mean; right, positive = higher). The page-24 figure title itself does not repeat 'Expected - Observed', and the caption describes residuals from predicted rates of the mixed model, which suggests a random-effect departure where positive = higher. So the index label is the likely slip, but the two statements are contradictory as printed. The figure supports only the qualitative statement of between-hospital heterogeneity, which is direction-invariant, and no hospital-level values are extractable, so I rate it minor_presentation with unlikely downstream impact.

rows.R: eTable 1 p.17: LDL difference 9.0 (3.2-14.8) is wider than pooled-SD calc with header n (4.30-13.70) that reproduces the other 5 rows, but LDL was measured in only 69% (Table 1: 14830/21374); implied missing-group LDL n about 193 (65%). Explained by variable-specific n.
rows.evidence: joi170166supp3_prod.pdf p.17 eTable 1; jama_huffman_2018_oi_170166.pdf p.5 Table 1 LDL n. Text layer. R script p1_c006.R.
rows.rationale: Recomputed in R (z interval, pooled SD, header n 21079 vs 295): age -1.99 to 0.79 (printed -2.0 to 0.8), weight -2.01 to 0.21 (-2.0 to 0.2), SBP -2.93 to 3.73 (-2.9 to 3.7), HR 0.83 to 5.17 (0.8 to 5.2), Hb -0.23 to 0.23 (-0.3 to 0.2, consistent with an unrounded difference slightly below 0), LDL 4.30 to 13.70 vs printed 3.2 to 14.8. Weight, SBP, HR and Hb are nearly complete in Table 1 (n >= 20842 of 21374), but LDL is available for 7288 + 7542 = 14830 (69.4%). Using pooled SD with total LDL n 14830, a half-width of 5.8 implies about 193 missing-follow-up participants with LDL (65.5% of 295), close to the overall availability. The wider LDL interval is therefore what one expects from the LDL-specific denominator; the table only omits per-variable n. No reporting error established, so exclude. Separately (not this candidate): the eTable 1 footnote says 'Difference = intervention minus control' although the columns are complete vs missing follow-up and the differences are missing minus complete.

rows.R: SAP p.6 (7.2) plans complete-case and multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses for missing outcomes. Report (p.7) gives MI and hypothetical-scenario results only; no result labelled complete case. Primary model may itself be complete case (295 missing), but this is not stated.
rows.evidence: joi170166supp2_prod.pdf p.6 7.1-7.2, p.7 7.5; main pdf p.3, p.4 Figure 1, p.6 follow-up paragraph, p.7 Primary Analysis and Table 3; joi170166supp3_prod.pdf p.17, p.21-23 (searched all supplement 3 text for 'complete'). Text layer.
rows.rationale: The SAP names two sensitivity analyses for missing outcomes: complete case and multiple imputation. The report states results were similar after multiple imputation and describes hypothetical-scenario sensitivity analyses, but nowhere identifies a complete-case analysis. Of 21374 eligible participants 295 (215 + 80) lacked outcome data; Table 3 uses arm totals 10066 + 11308 = 21374 as denominators for event percentages (645/10066 = 6.41%), so missing outcomes appear in the denominators as non-events in the descriptive rows. A mixed logistic model cannot use missing outcomes, so the primary model may be the complete-case analysis de facto, but the report does not say so. A planned sensitivity analysis is not identifiable in the report; retain. L indeterminate because the primary model may already be complete case.

rows.R: Final protocol V1.4/V2 p.71 (amendment table p.110) adds: survival with the same pre-arrest neurological disability counts as favorable. Related observation, not this candidate's claim: the final protocol defines technique failure as a composite of 28-day mortality, regurgitation or procedural failure, whereas the report's 'BMV or ETI failure' (69/1028 vs 21/996) is procedural failure only.

Report gives ITT/PP primary, ITT/PP secondary, safety in as-treated only, and no OR intervals; eTable 2 post hoc reclassification is not a full AT analysis.
rows.evidence: joi180004supp1_prod.pdf p.121 5.3, p.124 8.2; p.130 and p.133 scanned copies OCR'd at 300 dpi; main pdf p.1, p.3-4, p.6 Tables 2-3; joi180004supp2_prod.pdf p.3 eTable 2. Searched main text for 'as treated' and 'odds ratio'.

The report presents ITT and PP results; the only treatment-received-like analysis is a post hoc ITT reclassification of patients intubated after BMV before ROSC (41/863 vs 45/1174), which is labelled post hoc and is not the planned AT set. rows.R: Main p.4: 'The lower limit of the confidence interval was greater than the threshold of noninferiority, thus noninferiority was not demonstrated'; the lower limit -1.64% is below the -1% margin. Recomputed 44/1018 vs 43/1022: RD 0.11, Wald 95% lower bound -1.64, P(NI) 0.106. Wording reversed; conclusion correct.
rows.evidence: jama_jabre_2018_oi_180004.pdf p.1 abstract, p.3 Statistical Analysis, p.4 Primary Outcome, p.7 Discussion. Text layer. R script p2.R.
rows.rationale: Recomputed: 4.32% vs 4.21%, difference 0.11 points, Wald lower limit -1.64 (matches printed 1-sided 97.5% bound), one-sided P for NI against -1% = 0.106 (printed .11). Because -1.64 < -1, the sentence calling the lower limit greater than the threshold reverses the ordering, yet the same sentence and the abstract, Key Points and Discussion conclude correctly that NI was not shown. A confirmed wording error with no effect on the extracted estimate or conclusion: minor_presentation, unlikely downstream impact.

rows.R: Table 2 p.6 PP rows. Survival 28 d 54/995 vs 51/943: Wald RD 0.02 (-2.00 to 2.04), Newcombe -2.03 to 2.05; printed 0.1 (-10 to 9.7). Admission 289/995 vs 312/943: -4.04 (-8.16 to 0.08); printed -4.0 (-7.6 to 0.6). ITT rows reproduce exactly.
rows.evidence: jama_jabre_2018_oi_180004.pdf p.6 Table 2 and footnote, p.3 methods, p.4 text. Text layer; R scripts p2.R and p2c.R.
rows.rationale: Using the same Wald method that reproduces the ITT rows (survival 0.12, -1.83 to 2.07 vs printed 0.1, -1.8 to 2.1; admission -3.70, -7.70 to 0.30 vs -3.7, -7.7 to 0.3; ROSC -4.66, -8.83 to -0.49 vs -4.7, -8.8 to -0.5), the PP survival interval should be about -2.0 to 2.0; the printed -10 to 9.7 is roughly five times too wide. The PP admission interval should be -8.2 to 0.1; printed -7.6 to 0.6 is asymmetric about -4.0 (-3.6/+4.6), which no standard method gives; Newcombe score intervals also do not reproduce it. Chi-square P values for these rows (0.985 and 0.055) agree with the printed .99 and .055, so only the intervals are wrong. These are extractable per-protocol effect intervals, so substantive and direct.

rows.R: Table 2 p.6 PP ROSC ETI '377 (30.0)': 377/943 = 39.98%, so 40.0% expected. Printed difference -5.6 matches 34.4 - 40.0 (computed -5.61) and P .01 matches chi-square 0.011. Percentage typo; printed 30.0 would reverse direction.
rows.evidence: jama_jabre_2018_oi_180004.pdf p.6 Table 2; p.4 Figure (PP n = 943). Text layer. R script p2.R.
rows.rationale: 342/995 = 34.37% (printed 34.4). 377/943 = 39.98%, not 30.0%. Difference computed -5.61 (Wald CI -9.91 to -1.31), matching printed -5.6 (-9.9 to -1.3), and chi-square P = 0.011 (printed .01), so count, difference, CI and P are mutually consistent and only the ETI percentage is wrong. Taken alone, 30.0% vs 34.4% would invert the direction. Because the count, difference and text agree with each other, the intended value is recoverable: minor_presentation, with possible downstream impact if the percentage is extracted directly.

rows.R: Signed SAP p.130 (scanned; OCR and rendered crop viewed) prints H1: pi_BVM - pi_TI >= 0.01 without the minus sign; native SAP p.121 and the protocol copies print >= -0.01. H0 on the same signed page is <= -0.01 and 8.2.1 (p.133) uses lower limit > -0.01, so the intended margin is clear.
rows.evidence: joi180004supp1_prod.pdf p.121 (text), p.130 (scanned; OCR 300 dpi and cropped render viewed), p.124/p.133, protocol hypothesis lines (text layer search).
rows.rationale: The rendered signed copy clearly shows 'H1: pi BVM - pi TI >= 0.01'. Both copies have the same date (18 Feb 2015). The signed copy's own H0 (<= -0.01) and its operational rule (lower 95% CI limit higher than -0.01), plus the native copy and the protocols, all use -0.01; H1 with +0.01 would not be the complement of H0. The discrepancy is real but is a dropped minus sign whose intended meaning is unambiguous from the surrounding text, and the reported analysis used -1%. minor_presentation.

rows.R: Supp2 eTable 2 p.3: ECMO/donation-excluded row 43/971 vs 39/978, printed 0.4 [-2.2, 1.3]. Wald gives 0.44 (-1.34 to 2.22), Newcombe -1.37 to 2.26; printed limits look mirrored. Companion row 41/863 vs 45/1174 reproduces (0.92, -0.88 to 2.71 vs 0.9 [-0.9, 2.7]).
rows.evidence: joi180004supp2_prod.pdf p.3 eTable 2; main pdf p.3-4, p.6 post hoc text. Text layer; R scripts p2b.R, p2c.R.
rows.rationale: Exclusions reconcile: 1018 - 971 = 47 = 35 ECMO + 12 donation; 1022 - 978 = 44 = 23 + 21; total 91 as stated in the text. The printed interval [-2.2, 1.3] contains the point estimate but is asymmetric (-2.6/+0.9), whereas Wald and Newcombe intervals are about -1.3 to 2.2; the printed values match these with the signs and order reversed. The companion row reproduces with Wald, so the method is identified. P value 0.63 matches uncorrected chi-square 0.628. The interval is wrong as printed; the row is a post hoc sensitivity analysis, significance status is unchanged and the corrected interval is easily inferred, so minor_presentation with possible downstream impact. Initially I misread the interval as excluding the point estimate; on recheck (and as the card notes) it does contain 0.4.

rows.R: Abstract p.1, text p.6, Table 3 p.7: SCDE 'adjusted' RD -0.34 (-0.73 to 0.05) (implied P 0.088) printed with P = .03, which matches the RR 0.77 (0.61-0.97) (implied P 0.027). Footnote a says the SCDE RD was not baseline adjusted. Different models; P attribution not stated.
rows.evidence: jama_parshuram_2018_oi_180015.pdf p.1 abstract, p.5 methods (identity-link fallback), p.6 Secondary Outcome, p.7 Table 3 SCDE row and footnotes a, f. Text layer; R script p3.R.
rows.rationale: Back-calculated P values: RR 0.77 (0.61-0.97) gives P = 0.027, matching .03; RD -0.34 (-0.73 to 0.05) gives P = 0.088. Rates reproduce: 127/251859 = 0.50 and 259/307584 = 0.84 per 1000 patient-days. Methods (p.5) and footnote a state that when the identity-link GEE did not converge the RD came from a model without baseline adjustment, and SCDE is one of those outcomes; footnote f ties the RR to the baseline-adjusted Poisson model. So the conflict is explained by two different models and the primary inference (RR) is clear. Remaining reporting problem: the abstract and text label the RD 'adjusted' and place a single P value after both estimates without saying it belongs to the RR, so a reader sees an interval including 0 with P = .03. A presentation issue rather than a computational error: probable_issue, minor_presentation.

rows.R: Disclosed (main p.3-4). Protocol p.12, p.14, p.16 plans counts of each sign in the preceding 24 h and the number of times all 7 items were documented; report Table 2 (p.6) analyzes the last observation set with >=5 of 7 types.
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf p.12, p.14, p.16; jama_parshuram_2018_oi_180015.pdf p.3-4, p.6 Table 2; joi180015supp3_prod.pdf p.4-5 eFigure 2. Text layer.

The report states that before analysis the method was revised to use only the last set of observations and a threshold of 5 rather than 7. This changes the outcome definition (unit and threshold). Disclosure does not remove the difference.

rows.R: Protocol Table 5 (p.24) SCDE circulatory category needs >60 mL/kg fluid AND inotrope, and ward death without DNR. Report p.4: fluid >=60 mL/kg OR vasoactive drug, plus death within the first ICU hour; eTable 1 (supp3 p.6) says >60 mL/kg and/or inotrope. Composite definition changed; fluid boundary also differs within the report.
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf p.10-11, p.24 Table 5; jama_parshuram_2018_oi_180015.pdf p.4; joi180015supp3_prod.pdf p.6 eTable 1. Text layer.

Reported: any of intubation, vasoactive medication or fluid >=60 mL/kg within 12 h before ICU admission (either alone qualifies), CPR, ECMO, or death within the first ICU hour. Making fluid or inotrope individually sufficient and adding early-ICU death widen the composite; the report also gives >=60 (main text) vs >60 (eTable 1). This is a change in the definition of the main secondary outcome.

Report Table 3 (p.7) groups these under 'Post hoc Outcomes' (fn g, exploratory) and p.4 says PIM2 score was not prespecified, while also calling some of them prespecified.

The report's Methods list some of the same outcomes among the 21 prespecified outcomes, so the status labels conflict with the protocol and partly with the report's own text. rows.R: Protocol p.16: weighted hospital-level logit regression with treatment, baseline logit and size stratum. SAP p.1-4 and report p.4-5: GEE binomial/Poisson with treatment and baseline only; stratification removed (disclosed p.5, only 3 hospitals >=200 beds).

The SAP and the report use exchangeable GEE logistic/Poisson models with intervention and baseline value, and the report states that stratification was removed. Model class, weighting and covariate set differ; removal of strata is disclosed. The report matches the SAP, which is undated and written in the past tense.

rows.R: Disclosed (p.5 and Table 3 fn a). SAP p.2-3 specifies identity-link Poisson GEE with baseline rate for absolute effects; SCDE RD was estimated without baseline adjustment after nonconvergence.
rows.evidence: joi180015supp2_prod.pdf p.2-3; joi180015supp1_prod.pdf p.16; jama_parshuram_2018_oi_180015.pdf p.1, p.5, p.7 Table 3 fn a. Text layer.

Footnote a lists SCDE among outcomes whose RD model was not adjusted for baseline, a fallback described on p.5. The planned covariate adjustment was dropped for the key secondary outcome's RD; disclosed nonconvergence is context, not grounds for exclusion.

rows.R: Disclosed (p.5): protocol p.16 lists 4 a priori subgroups and SAP p.6 two (ECMO, MET) with interaction tests; report says the planned subgroup analyses are not reported. None found in main text or supp3.
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf p.16; joi180015supp2_prod.pdf p.6; jama_parshuram_2018_oi_180015.pdf p.5; joi180015supp3_prod.pdf full text searched for 'subgroup'. Text layer.

rows.R: Table 2 p.6 respiratory rate 0.85 (0.02 to 1.68), P = .05, Holm-adjusted P = .18. CI is unadjusted for multiplicity; the separate Holm column is expected to be larger. CI-implied P = 0.045, compatible with printed .05. No inconsistency.
rows.evidence: jama_parshuram_2018_oi_180015.pdf p.5 multiplicity methods, p.6 Table 2 row and footnotes c-d. Text layer; R script p3.R.
rows.rationale: The interval and the raw P value come from the same GEE model; the back-calculated P from the interval is 0.045, consistent with .05 after rounding of the limits. The Holm-adjusted P value is labelled in its own column and is not meant to agree with an unadjusted 95% CI. A CI excluding zero with a nonsignificant multiplicity-adjusted P is the expected pattern, not a reporting error.

rows.R: Protocol p.16 secondary analysis (d): logit model for all-cause mortality following DNR orders. No modeled after-DNR result; after-DNR counts derivable (97-42 = 55; 147-47 = 100).
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf p.10, p.16; jama_parshuram_2018_oi_180015.pdf p.6, p.7 Table 3, p.9; joi180015supp3_prod.pdf p.9 eTable 2. Text layer; R script p3.R.

The report models mortality without a DNR order, the complementary subset; deaths after DNR are only derivable by subtraction (55 and 100 in the intervention period; 155 overall, matching the reported 155 deaths after DNR orders). The limitations paragraph describes the analysis as one of 'mortality after DNR order', which may mean excluding after-DNR deaths. rows.R: Protocol p.14 (2.11): 18% RRR = absolute risk reduction 0.09%; power appendix p.29: 'absolute risk reduction of 0.9%'. 0.178 x 5.1/1000 = 0.91/1000 = 0.091%, so the appendix should read 0.9 per 1000; protocol p.1 and report p.4 use 0.9/1000.
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf p.1, p.14, p.29; jama_parshuram_2018_oi_180015.pdf p.4. Text layer; R script p3.R.
rows.rationale: Computed 0.178 x 5.1 per 1000 = 0.908 per 1000 = 0.091%. The body value (0.09%) is correct; the appendix percentage is off by a factor of 10 (per-1000 value with a % sign). Other plan locations and the report give 0.9 per 1000, so the intended effect size is clear: a real but presentational inconsistency within the plan.

rows.R: SAP p.4-5 'Sensitivity to model choice' lists GLMER, post-only, pre/post interaction, weighted-linear and quasi-likelihood models for ORs, RRs and RDs. No such sensitivity results in the main report or supp3 (searched).
rows.evidence: joi180015supp2_prod.pdf p.4-5; jama_parshuram_2018_oi_180015.pdf p.4-7; joi180015supp3_prod.pdf full text searched (sensitiv, mixed, GLMER). Text layer.

Only the baseline-adjusted GEE results are reported; no alternative-model estimates or robustness summary appear in the article or supplement. A planned sensitivity analysis for the primary and key secondary outcomes is not reported. The SAP's past tense suggests it may document completed checks, which does not change the absence in the report.

rows.R: Table 2 p.6 (and abstract) RRs do not equal low/intermediate risk ratios: ARDS 17/448 vs 23/462 gives RR 0.76 (0.41-1.41), printed 0.86 (0.59-1.24); extrapulmonary infection 0.74 (0.42-1.29) vs 0.84 (0.60-1.18). All 10 printed RRs and CIs reproduce as P(low arm | event)/P(low arm | no event), i.e., a transposed 2x2 table. P values (chi-square) are correct.
rows.evidence: jama_simonis_2018_oi_180108.pdf p.1 abstract, p.4 methods, p.6 Table 2 all RR rows and footnote c; joi180108supp2_prod.pdf p.13 planned RR method. Text layer; R script p4.R.
rows.rationale: For each of the 10 binary rows I computed the arm-risk ratio with log-Wald CI and the uncorrected chi-square P. Crude RRs: ICU mortality 1.17 (0.94-1.45) vs printed 1.11 (0.96-1.27); hospital 1.09 vs 1.06; ARDS 0.76 (0.41-1.41) vs 0.86 (0.59-1.24); pneumonia 1.15 vs 1.07; pneumothorax 1.37 (0.48-3.93) vs 1.16 (0.73-1.84); atelectasis 1.01 vs 1.00; extrapulmonary infection 0.74 vs 0.84; sepsis 0.78 vs 0.87; delirium 1.19 (0.99-1.42) vs 1.15 (0.99-1.34); tracheostomy 1.05 vs 1.03. Chi-square P values (0.153, 0.357, 0.384, 0.674, 0.551, 0.942, 0.285, 0.497, 0.063, 0.775) match the printed P values, so the counts are right. The ratio of the proportion in the low-tidal-volume arm among patients with vs without the event, with its log-Wald CI, reproduces every printed RR and CI (e.g., ARDS 0.858 (0.59-1.24); ICU 1.111 (0.96-1.28); delirium 1.156 (0.99-1.34)). The printed estimates are therefore not risk ratios of low vs intermediate tidal volume; they are attenuated toward 1 with intervals that are too narrow. This affects all abstract and Table 2 RRs, which are directly extractable. The card flagged only ARDS and extrapulmonary infection as beyond display precision and left the estimator open; my recomputation identifies the estimator and extends the issue to all 10 rows.

rows.R: Protocol p.28 collects 'moderate or severe ARDS (yes/no)' daily; protocol endpoint p.26, SAP p.9 and report p.4 (Berlin ref) say 'development of (new) ARDS', and protocol Appendix (p.48) includes mild. Whether reported ARDS (17/448 vs 23/462) includes mild cases cannot be determined.
rows.evidence: joi180108supp1_prod.pdf p.18, p.26, p.28, p.48; joi180108supp2_prod.pdf p.9; jama_simonis_2018_oi_180108.pdf p.1, p.4, p.6 Table 2. Text layer.

If the collection form governed, the reported outcome is moderate/severe ARDS; if not, the definition was broadened. The materials do not settle which, so the planned and reported definitions may differ but the nature of the difference is indeterminate.

rows.R: Protocol p.17-18 excludes patients with PaO2/FiO2 <200 mm Hg unless the attending states no ARDS and no direct risk factor. SAP p.6-7 and report p.2 exclude only Berlin-defined ARDS. Table 1 median PaO2/FiO2 197 (low) and 195 (intermediate), and eTable 5 has a <=200 subgroup.

With baseline medians below 200 in both arms, about half the enrolled patients had values that the protocol would generally have excluded unless the exception applied; how many met the exception is not reported. The eligibility criteria differ in a way that bears on the trial population.

rows.R: Protocol p.10, p.19, p.33: VFD at day 28 'after ICU admission'; protocol p.26 and SAP p.8: 'day 1 to day 28'; report p.4: calculated from randomization. rows.evidence: joi180108supp1_prod.pdf p.10, p.19, p.26, p.33; joi180108supp2_prod.pdf p.8; jama_simonis_2018_oi_180108.pdf p.4-6. Text layer.

For an outcome counted in whole days, this difference is unlikely to change the measure. A real but minor difference in wording of the definition: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Disclosed (main p.2; SAP modification table p.21). Protocol p.33 planned Cox regression for the primary VFD outcome; SAP p.12 and report p.4/Table 2 use Student t test and mean difference.
rows.evidence: joi180108supp1_prod.pdf p.19, p.33; joi180108supp2_prod.pdf p.12, p.21-22; jama_simonis_2018_oi_180108.pdf p.2, p.4, p.6 Table 2. Text layer.

The protocol's own power calculation used a two-group t test, but its analysis section specifies Cox regression. The change is disclosed; the primary analysis model differs.

Only the GLMM with stratification variables (P = .72) is reported. Planned primary-outcome analyses not reported: substantive_difference; partly disclosed.

rows.R: Disclosed in SAP modification table p.22 ('change the zero-inflated distribution to Gaussian'). SAP p.14 planned subgroup interactions by zero-inflated GLM; report p.4 and eTable 5 use Gaussian GLM.
rows.evidence: joi180108supp2_prod.pdf p.14, p.22; jama_simonis_2018_oi_180108.pdf p.4, p.6; joi180108supp3_prod.pdf p.9 eTable 5 (rendered). Text layer.

rows.R: Supp3 eTable 2 p.6 (rendered): Other mode, after titration, intermediate-arm PEEP '8 (5 - 1)'. A third quartile of 1 cannot lie below a median of 8; likely a truncated value (e.g., 10).
rows.evidence: joi180108supp3_prod.pdf p.6 eTable 2 rendered at 150 dpi and viewed.

It concerns a descriptive ventilator setting in a small subgroup (n = 28) on one day and does not affect the main results: minor_presentation, unlikely downstream impact.

rows.R: Supp3 eTable 5 p.9 (rendered): 'Ventilation before randomization' block prints two value rows against the heading line and '>6 hours', with '<=6 hours' blank. Row 1 CI width 13.5 days, row 2 width 3.0; given median pre-randomization ventilation 0.9 h, row 1 is probably >6 h, but labels are misaligned.
rows.evidence: joi180108supp3_prod.pdf p.9 eTable 5 rendered at 150 dpi and viewed; jama_simonis_2018_oi_180108.pdf p.4, p.5 Table 1.
rows.rationale: Row 1: 16.5 vs 16.8, -0.29 (-7.04 to 6.45); row 2: 15.2 vs 15.4, -0.21 (-1.72 to 1.28). Differences reproduce (16.5-16.8 = -0.3; 15.2-15.4 = -0.2). As printed, the >6 h label sits beside row 2 and the <=6 h label beside nothing. Because almost all patients were ventilated <1 h before randomization (Table 1 median 0.9 h), the much wider interval must belong to the small >6 h subgroup, so the intended mapping is recoverable with context; the interaction P (.98) is unaffected. A real layout inconsistency with recoverable meaning: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Supp3 eTable 4 p.8 (rendered) is titled 'during the first three days' but days of vasopressor use are 2 (1-4) in both arms. Q3 = 4 is compatible only with calendar-day counting of randomization day plus days 1-3 (as in eTable 2 columns); sedative/analgesic days are fractional. Window and unit not stated.
rows.evidence: joi180108supp3_prod.pdf p.5-8 eTables 1-4 (rendered and viewed); jama_simonis_2018_oi_180108.pdf p.4, p.6.

The sedative and analgesic durations are fractional (e.g., 0.6 days), suggesting elapsed time, whereas vasopressor days are integers, suggesting calendar-day counts. The table does not define the counting rule, so whether there is a conflict cannot be established: indeterminate.

rows.R: Abstract p.1 lists 'PaO2:FIO2 ratio over the 3 days after intubation' and reports 150 vs 119; main p.6 says PaO2:FIO2 was higher 'until day 4 (150 vs 119)'; supp2 eTable p.2 gives 150 vs 119 as the ratio 6 hours after randomization; eFigure 2B x-axis is time from randomization.

Intubation and randomization are different time origins, and most patients were never intubated (150 and 170 IMV). A reader cannot tell which time point and origin the extracted result refers to, so the conflict is substantive.

rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf p.98-99; jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.2, p.4 Table 1, p.5, p.7 Figure 3 (rendered at 170 dpi and viewed).

Figure 3 uses ICU time 0-1 vs >=2 days (Table 1 counts 244+77 = 321 and 47+20 = 67 confirm this split) and oxygen <=9 vs >9, so patients at exactly 2 days and exactly 9 L/min change subgroup. The subgroup definitions of the 'predefined' analyses changed: substantive_difference.

rows.R: Final SAP p.99: 'HFNO will not be used in the control group.' Report p.3 allows HFNO for control patients with do-not-intubate orders after standard oxygen failure; p.5: 30 control patients (7.7%) switched to HFNO.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf p.99; jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.3, p.3 Figure 1, p.5 Interventions. Text layer.

This changes the control-arm procedure and introduces crossover: substantive_difference.

rows.R: Final SAP p.103 secondary outcomes include dyspnea by VAS and Borg scale and oxygenation by lowest SpO2 and PaO2/FiO2. Report and supp2 give dyspnea VAS and PaO2/FiO2 only; no Borg or lowest-SpO2 results found.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf p.38, p.46, p.90, p.103; jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.1, p.3-4, p.6; joi180109supp2_prod.pdf p.2-5 (full text searched for Borg, lowest, SpO2).

Planned outcome measures not reported: substantive_difference, though the domains (dyspnea, oxygenation) are covered by other measures.

rows.R: Final SAP p.104 (and original SAP p.82): primary effect as relative risk of death with 95% CI, adjusted analyses, and a per-protocol analysis. Report gives risk difference and univariable Cox HR (p.3, Table 2 p.5), no RR, no adjusted or per-protocol primary result; p.8 limitation notes effects were not adjusted.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf p.53-54, p.82, p.104; jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.3-8; joi180109supp2_prod.pdf p.1-5. Text layer.
rows.rationale: The planned primary effect measure (RR) is replaced by RD and HR, and the planned adjusted and per-protocol analyses of the primary outcome are absent. The lack of adjustment is acknowledged in Limitations (disclosed). Primary analysis specification differs.

rows.R: Final SAP p.105: ICU-acquired events (intubation, infection) by cumulative incidence with death or ICU discharge alive as competing events, Gray test, cause-specific Cox adjusted for confounders. Report p.3-4: IMV with death without IMV as only competing risk; infections compared by chi-square; univariable cause-specific HRs (Table 2).
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf p.54, p.82, p.105; jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.3-6 Table 2 fn d. Text layer.
rows.rationale: The competing-event set (ICU discharge alive omitted), the analysis of infections (chi-square of proportions instead of competing-risk cumulative incidence) and the adjustment (none instead of confounder-adjusted) differ from the plan. These are analysis differences for key secondary outcomes.

rows.R: Methods p.4: IMV cumulative incidence compared with the Gray test; supp2 eFigure 1 p.3 (rendered) labels the same comparison 'P (log Rank test) = 0.17'; Table 2 prints P = .17 beside the cause-specific HR.
rows.evidence: jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.3-6; joi180109supp2_prod.pdf p.3 eFigure 1 (rendered 110 dpi and viewed).
rows.rationale: The test producing P = .17 is named as the Gray test in Methods and as a log-rank test on the figure. These tests address different quantities (subdistribution cumulative incidence vs cause-specific hazard) and can give different P values, though here they share a single printed value. The naming conflict is real but the inference (no significant difference) is unchanged: confirmed_issue, minor_presentation.

rows.R: Table 1 p.4 (n = 388 per arm): HFNO liver 45 (13.3), control kidney 69 (20.4), postextubation 14 (4.1) and 18 (5.3). With 388: 11.6%, 17.8%, 3.6%, 4.6%; all four printed values equal count/338. Other cells reproduce with 388.

The four flagged cells reproduce exactly with 338 (45/338 = 13.3, 69/338 = 20.4, 14/338 = 4.1, 18/338 = 5.3), while their same-row companions use 388 (e.g., control liver 56/388 = 14.4), so missing data are an unlikely explanation and a denominator slip is likely. Counts appear correct and the percentages are off by 0.5-2.6 points in baseline descriptors: minor_presentation, possible downstream impact if percentages are extracted.

rows.R: Final SAP p.105 (original SAP p.82): longitudinal oxygenation, dyspnea and comfort to be analyzed with joint models accounting for right censoring. Report p.4 uses Wilcoxon rank-sum tests at time points; supp2 eFigures 2-3 show descriptive trajectories with shrinking n.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf p.55, p.82, p.105; jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.1, p.4, p.6; joi180109supp2_prod.pdf p.4-5. Text layer.

rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf p.54, p.82, p.105; jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.1, p.4, p.5 Table 2 fn e, p.6. Text layer.
rows.rationale: Both the estimator (KM/competing-risk vs Wilcoxon and mean difference) and the analysis populations (survivors and decedents separately) differ from the plan. Planned analyses of a secondary outcome not reported as specified.

rows.R: Disclosed redesign (main p.3). Initial grant protocol (supp1 p.6-7, p.38, p.45, p.47) lists mortality after intubation/HFNO failure as a secondary endpoint; final SAP list (p.103) omits it; report p.4 and p.6 present intubated-patient mortality as post hoc. Report is consistent with the final plan.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf p.1 (contents), p.6-7, p.38, p.45, p.47, p.103; jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.3, p.4, p.6, p.8. Text layer.
rows.rationale: The initial noninferiority protocol named mortality after intubation as a secondary outcome; the superiority redesign dropped it and the report labels the analysis post hoc. Under the review rule that disclosed changes are retained as differences, the outcome status differs between the supplied initial plan and the report, although the report agrees with the final SAP. Arithmetic of the reported difference checks: 55.3 - 52.3 = 3.0, printed +3%.

rows.R: Figure 3 p.7 (rendered) all-patient HRs are reciprocals of Table 2: mortality 1.02 (0.81-1.29) vs 0.98 (0.77-1.24); IMV 1.17 (0.94-1.46) vs 0.85 (0.68-1.06). So forest HRs are standard vs HFNO, yet HR < 1 is labelled 'favors high-flow'. E.g., IMV non-hematologic 61/199 (30.7%) vs 89/198 (44.9%) plotted as HR 1.61 on the 'favors standard' side.
rows.evidence: jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.4 methods, p.5 Table 2, p.6, p.7 Figure 3 both panels (rendered at 170 dpi and viewed). R script p5.R.
rows.rationale: 1/0.98 = 1.020, 1/1.24 = 0.806, 1/0.77 = 1.299; 1/0.85 = 1.176, 1/1.06 = 0.943, 1/0.68 = 1.471, matching the Figure 3 all-patient rows, so the figure's HR contrast is the inverse of Table 2's. The favors headings were not reversed: HR > 1 now means lower hazard with HFNO but is plotted under 'favors standard'. Raw counts confirm the direction: in the only significant interaction (hematologic malignancy, IMV, P = .01), the non-hematologic subgroup had 30.7% IMV with HFNO vs 44.9% with standard oxygen, yet its HR 1.61 (1.16-2.23) sits on the side labelled as favoring standard oxygen. Every subgroup direction in both panels is mislabelled: confirmed, substantive, direct.

rows.R: Table 2 p.5 ICU-acquired infection 39/388 vs 41/388, cause-specific HR 1.01 (0.96 to 1.06). With 80 events SE(log HR) is about sqrt(1/39+1/41) = 0.224, giving roughly 0.65-1.57; printed interval implies SE 0.025. Same construction reproduces the mortality and IMV rows.
rows.evidence: jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.1 abstract, p.4, p.5 Table 2 and fn d. Text layer; R script p5.R.
rows.rationale: An HR interval of 0.96-1.06 requires about 6000 events; the arm counts give 80. The event-count approximation reproduces the printed mortality (0.77-1.24) and IMV (0.68-1.06) intervals, so the infection interval is not a plausible output of the stated model. The HR point estimate is also hard to reconcile with crude proportions 10.1% vs 10.6% (RR 0.95), though competing-risk weighting could move it. The printed interval overstates precision by about ninefold and would be extracted directly. Related observation: the infection risk difference -0.6 (-4.6 to 4.1) and P = .91 do not reproduce with Wald/chi-square (-0.52, -4.79 to 3.76; P = 0.81).

rows.R: Main p.6: 'vasopressors and renal replacement therapy were needed in 153 patients (19.7%) randomized to high-flow ... and 31 patients (4%) randomized to standard oxygen ... with no statistical difference'. 153/776 = 19.7% and 31/776 = 4.0%: pooled percentages, apparently vasopressors and RRT overall, misattributed to arms.
rows.evidence: jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.3 Figure 1, p.5 Patients, p.6 Post Hoc Outcomes. Text layer; R script p5.R.
rows.rationale: Against arm denominators of 388, 153 would be 39.4% and 31 would be 8.0%; the printed percentages equal the counts over all 776 patients. A 153 vs 31 split between arms would also contradict 'no statistical difference'. The most plausible reading is 153 patients needing vasopressors and 31 needing RRT across both arms, so the sentence mislabels outcomes as arms and arm-specific values are not given. The sentence as printed would mislead an extractor and the true arm data are unavailable: confirmed, substantive.

rows.R: Figure 3 p.7 (rendered): PaO2:FIO2 subgroups total 302 (HFNO) and 286 (standard) of 388; hematologic malignancy No+Yes = 366 and 379, and deaths 130 and 137 vs 138 and 140; Table 1 gives 167/181 with malignancy, implying 221/207 without. Other subgroup pairs sum to 388. Exclusions not explained; Methods state no exclusions for missing data.

This contradicts the statement that no participants were excluded because of missing data unless the figure used a different definition, which is not stated. Likely a reporting issue, but an undisclosed alternative definition remains possible: probable_issue. The interval estimates themselves are not shown to be wrong; impact limited to subgroup interpretation (although the hematologic IMV interaction is the only significant one).

rows.R: Figure 3 title (p.7) calls all subgroups 'predefined', including unknown diagnosis and hematologic malignancy (and PaO2:FIO2). The final SAP p.98-99 and p.104 define subgroup interactions only on the three stratification factors; methods p.4 also lists only stratification variables. No plan basis found for the two added subgroups.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf p.45-46, p.53, p.82, p.98-99, p.104 (searched); jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.4, p.5, p.7 Figure 3 (rendered).

Unknown diagnosis, hematologic malignancy and PaO2:FIO2 subgroups appear in a figure titled 'predefined subgroups' without a supplied prospective specification, and the main text refers to '3 predefined subgroups'. Analyses described as prespecified are not in the supplied plan: substantive_difference.

rows.R: Report (abstract p.1; p.3) states temperature was managed in both groups for 7 days. Final protocol V9 p.77 limits control-arm pyrexia control to 96 h post randomization and Appendix F p.101 keeps rewarmed hypothermia patients normothermic for 96 h (12.11 says up to 7 days).

The duration of protocolized temperature control is a procedural element of the comparator: substantive_difference.

rows.R: Abstract p.1 prints 'risk difference, 0.4% [95% CI, -9.4% to 8.7%]'; main p.5 and Table 2 p.7 print -0.4. Recomputed 117/240 - 111/226 = -0.37 points (Wald -9.4 to 8.7). Abstract sign dropped.

The abstract's positive 0.4 is a sign omission; the CI and the stated percentages make the intended value clear, and the conclusion is unaffected, but an extractor using the abstract would take the wrong sign: minor_presentation, possible downstream impact.

rows.R: Final protocol synopsis p.69: 33C 'maintained ... for a further 72 hours' after target; 12.11 p.77 and flowchart p.99: rewarming assessed 72 h after randomization, with a 48 h cooling minimum if cooling started late. Report p.3: at least 72 h after randomization; late-start minimum not mentioned.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf p.69, p.77, p.97, p.99; jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf p.3-4. Text layer.

The main conflict lies within the plan; the plan-report difference is limited to omission of a conditional rule. minor_presentation.

rows.R: Report p.3: rewarming 'at a target rate up to 0.25C/h' (original 2009 protocol rate). Final protocol V9 p.77, p.99-100: 0.17C/h (0.5C every 3 h). Reported median rewarming 22.5 h for 33-37C (about 0.18C/h) fits the final protocol.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf p.21 (V1 12.11, 0.25C/h), p.77, p.99-100; jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf p.1, p.3-4. Text layer.

The difference is in the stated target rather than in apparent conduct: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Final protocol p.84 and V8 amendment p.174-175: modified ITT excludes consent withdrawals and patients not meeting inclusion criteria who never received the intervention. Report p.3-4: analyses by randomized group excluding only consent withdrawals (500 of 511). Ineligible patients were excluded only from per-protocol/as-treated sets (supp2 p.12, p.17).
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf p.84, p.174-175; jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf p.3-4 Figure 1; joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.12, p.17. Text layer.
rows.rationale: The amended plan defines the primary analysis population more narrowly than the report. The number of randomized patients who were ineligible and never treated is not reported, so the size of the difference is unknown, but the population definitions differ.

rows.R: Final protocol p.84: primary dichotomized GOSE to be reported as RR, RD and OR with 95% CIs. Report gives RR and RD only (p.1, p.5, Table 2); ORs in supp2 p.22 are post hoc for a different subset. Planned primary OR not reported (derivable from counts).
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf p.84; jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf p.1, p.3, p.5, p.7; joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.1-24 searched for 'odds ratio'. Text layer.
rows.rationale: One of three planned effect measures for the primary outcome is absent. The counts allow an OR to be computed, and the published SAP that may have fixed the reporting format is cited but not supplied, so I record the difference without characterizing its importance (L left blank).

rows.R: Methods p.4: Cox model censored at 6 months; supp2 eFigure 2 p.5 (rendered) runs to 250 days with 91/88 at risk at 200 days and 23/17 at 250 days. Display contradicts the stated 6-month window; curves are flat after about 100 days.
rows.evidence: jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf p.2, p.4, p.5; joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.5 eFigure 2 rendered at 110 dpi and viewed.
rows.rationale: Six months is at most about 184 days, so administrative censoring at 6 months implies no patients at risk at 200 or 250 days; the figure shows positive risk sets and is labelled 'probability of death at 6 months'. Either the KM/log-rank (P = 0.5349) used full follow-up or the description is wrong. Because the curves are flat after the early weeks, any deaths beyond 6 months are few and the HR 1.13 (0.76-1.69) is unlikely to change materially: confirmed inconsistency, minor_presentation.

rows.R: Supp2 eTable 7 p.11: favorable outcome by time to 33C, 18/49, 28/67, 32/59, 39/65, P = .09 ('chi-square for equal proportions', main p.4). Pearson chi-square (3 df) on these counts P = 0.043; Fisher exact 0.044; excluding 'Never' 0.16; trend test 0.005. Printed .09 not reproduced; text p.5 calls it nonsignificant.
rows.evidence: jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf p.4 methods, p.5 Additional Outcomes; joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.11 eTable 7. Text layer; R one-liners (chisq.test, fisher.test, prop.trend.test).
rows.rationale: With integer counts summing to 240 (the hypothermia primary-outcome set), the stated test gives P = 0.043, not .09; no standard alternative reproduces .09. If the stated test was used, the main-text statement of no significant difference is wrong at the paper's 0.05 threshold. The card treated half-unit count ranges as reconciling, which I do not accept because counts are integers. Some undisclosed subset or test could produce .09, so probable rather than confirmed. Exploratory and confounded (patients never reaching 33C did best), but the significance statement would change: substantive.

rows.R: Final protocol p.84: with 11 Haybittle-Peto interim looks, final analysis at +/-1.996 SD (P = 0.0459). Report p.4: 2-sided P < .05. DSMC charter p.188: |Z3| >= 1.975 (P = .048) but final alpha 0.05. No reported P lies between 0.0459 and 0.05.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf p.84, p.188; jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf p.4. Text layer; R: 2*pnorm(-1.996) = 0.0459, 2*pnorm(-1.975) = 0.0483.
rows.rationale: The final-analysis significance threshold differs between plan (0.0459) and report (0.05), and the plan documents disagree among themselves (0.0459 vs 0.048 vs 0.05). This is a difference in the decision rule; it changes no reported conclusion because the primary P = .94 and no P value falls in the gap.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7: RR, CI and P for the two bleeding rows are swapped. Intracranial 47/260 vs 37/240: RR 1.17 (0.79-1.74), P 0.43 (printed 1.23 (0.43-3.5), .70); extracranial 8/260 vs 6/240: RR 1.23 (0.43-3.50), P 0.70 (printed 1.17 (0.79-1.74), .43). rows.evidence: jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf p.3, p.5, p.7 Table 2; joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.10 eTable 6. Text layer; R script p6.R.
rows.rationale: All other Table 2 rows reproduce with crude RR (log-Wald CI), Wald RD and uncorrected chi-square. For the bleeding rows the RD values (2.7 and 0.6) match their own counts, but the RR/CI/P triplets belong to the other row. eTable 6 lists P = .43 for intracranial and .70 for extracranial, agreeing with recomputation and contradicting Table 2. The intracranial bleeding RR is a key safety estimate and would be extracted with the wrong precision and P: substantive, direct.

rows.R: DSMC charter p.188: Haybittle-Peto |Zk| >= 3 boundary described as 'approximate P < 0.001'; |Z| = 3 corresponds to two-sided P = 0.0027 (P = 0.001 needs |Z| = 3.29). Earlier amendment p.152 (scanned; OCR) pairs the 3-SD rule with P < 0.005. Final protocol p.84 says 3SD.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf p.84 (text), p.152 (scanned; OCR 300 dpi), p.188 (text). R: 2*pnorm(-3) = 0.0027.
rows.rationale: The interim boundary is stated as 3 SD throughout, but its P-value equivalent is given as <0.001 in the charter and <0.005 in an earlier amendment, neither of which equals 0.0027. The plan materials therefore conflict on the numeric threshold. No interim analysis approached a boundary (trial completed; interim P values not near either), so the conflict does not affect reported results: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Supp1 p.192 (DSMC report, 17 July 2016; rendered): favorable-outcome table for group Y sums cumulatively to 7, 9, 20, ... 73, but the cumulative Y line plots about 6, 12, 17, 22, ... 80, which equals cumulative unfavorable counts (13-7, 8-2, 16-11, ...). X line matches favorable sums.

rows.R: Supp2 eTable 10 p.18 (as-treated baseline), normothermia (n = 196): Marshall V printed '34.7 (68)' and VI '1 (2)'. 68/196 = 34.7%, so count and percent are transposed; 1/196 = 0.5%, not 2.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.18 eTable 10. Text layer.

rows.R: Supp2 p.22 (rendered): adjusted OR printed '0.95 (0.55-275 1.64) P = .84'. The '275' is a stray token; intended interval is evidently 0.55-1.64.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.22 rendered at 110 dpi and viewed.
