rows.R: Final protocol p.85: sensitivity analyses of the primary and secondary outcomes adjusted for prespecified baseline covariates. Report gives an IMPACT-adjusted RR for the primary outcome only (Table 2; eTables 9, 11); no adjusted results for pneumonia, intracranial bleeding or other secondary outcomes. SAP update p.183-184 (scanned; OCR) concerns per-protocol/as-treated adjustments.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf p.84-85 (text), p.181, p.183-184, p.187 (scanned; OCR 300 dpi); jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf p.3-7; joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.10, p.14, p.19-22.
rows.rationale: Planned covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses of secondary outcomes are not reported in the supplied materials. The published SAP is cited only by reference (p.181) and not supplied, so it is unknown whether it narrowed the plan. Planned analyses absent: substantive_difference.

rows.R: Abstract p.1: '22% men'. Main p.4: 22 men and 8 women enrolled (22/30 = 73.3%); Table 1 p.5: 13 + 7 = 20 men among 27 completers (74%). Abstract percentage is wrong (apparently the count printed as a percent).
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.1, p.4, p.5 Table 1 (rendered 200 dpi); joi180136supp2_prod.pdf p.3-4 eTable 2.
rows.rationale: 22/30 = 73.3% men; the abstract's 22% inverts the sex composition (it would imply about 7 men). Sex distribution is a standard extracted baseline descriptor, and the abstract figure would be taken directly by an extractor, so substantive with direct impact, although it does not affect efficacy results.

rows.R: Protocol p.40-41: hierarchical model with patient random intercept/slope, centre and subgroup fixed; elicited clinical priors (overall effect N(1.75, 0.89) and per-patient priors) with a noninformative-prior robustness analysis. Supp2 eMethods 2-3 (p.11-14) use only vague priors (N with precision 0.001/0.01, uniform SDs) and separate placebo/mexiletine means; no clinical-prior analysis or robustness comparison reported.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf p.12, p.40-41; jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.3, p.4, p.6 Figure 3; joi180136supp2_prod.pdf p.10-14. Text layer.
rows.rationale: The planned primary Bayesian analysis used elicited clinical priors for the main parameters, with noninformative priors only as a sensitivity check; the reported models use vague priors only and a different parameterization (separate population means for each treatment, no centre term). Neither the clinical-prior analysis nor the robustness comparison is reported. Prior specification and model structure of the primary analysis differ.

rows.R: Protocol p.40: 'secondary endpoints will be analyzed in the same way' (Bayesian hierarchical model). Report p.3 and Table 2 p.7-8: non-IVR secondary outcomes analyzed by frequentist dependent t tests, labelled exploratory.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf p.7, p.31, p.40; jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.3-4, p.7-8 (rendered).
rows.rationale: The analysis framework for non-IVR secondary outcomes changed from the planned Bayesian hierarchical model to paired t tests; no Bayesian results are given for them. Analysis method differs.

rows.R: Protocol p.32-33: eyelid and handgrip myotonia after 3-second contraction; dynamometry relaxation measured as 90-10%, 90-50% and 90-75% of MVIC. Report p.3, Table 1 fn d, Table 2 fn h/j: 5-second contractions and a single 90%-5% relaxation time.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf p.32-33; jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.3, p.5, p.7-8 (rendered).
rows.rationale: The contraction duration for the bedside tests (3 s vs 5 s) and the relaxation-time definition (three planned cut-offs vs one 90%-5% measure) differ. These are measurement definitions of secondary outcomes.

rows.R: Protocol p.35: intent-to-treat; all data acquired before termination included in the primary analysis unless consent withdrawn. Report p.3: aggregated analysis includes patients completing at least 1 treatment period; n = 27, dropouts 3, 6, 7 (one SAE) absent from eTable 3 (supp2 p.5).
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf p.35; jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.3, p.4 Figure 1, p.8; joi180136supp2_prod.pdf p.5 eTable 3 (rendered 140 dpi).
rows.rationale: The plan includes partial data from withdrawn patients; the report restricts the primary analysis to patients completing at least one treatment period and analyzes 27 of 30. Whether the dropouts had usable IVR data is not stated, but the inclusion rule differs from the planned one.

rows.R: Protocol p.40: investigate treatment x pair and treatment x order interactions in the primary model. Report p.4 gives 'randomization order effect (P = .85)' and 'period effect (P = .22)' from the frequentist model; eMethods models contain no interaction terms. Unclear whether these are the planned interactions.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf p.40; jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.3-4; joi180136supp2_prod.pdf p.11-14. Text layer.
rows.rationale: The reported order and period terms are described as main-effect covariables in the frequentist model, not as interactions with treatment in the Bayesian model. In a crossover, an order effect can correspond to a treatment-by-period interaction, so the reported tests may or may not address the planned questions. The planned interaction analyses are not identifiable as such: indeterminate.

rows.R: Main p.4: in 3 patients 'Bayesian analysis showed the predefined clinical ineffectiveness'. Supp2 eTable 3 p.5 (rendered): patients 13 and 22 have posterior probabilities 2% and 1% (<20%), but patient 11 has 38%; its footnote explains a judgment-based stop. Only 2 met the rule.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.3, p.4; joi180136supp2_prod.pdf p.5 eTable 3 rendered at 140 dpi.
rows.rationale: The predefined nonresponse criterion is posterior probability <=20% (protocol) or <20% (eTable 3 footnote). Patient 11 (38%) does not meet it; the supplement discloses that the stop reflected absence of stiffness in both periods. The main text nevertheless attributes all three nonresponders to the predefined Bayesian criterion. The count of clinical nonresponders is unchanged and the explanation is available in the supplement: minor_presentation. Related observation: patients 8 and 20 are counted as responders at a displayed 80%, which meets the protocol's 'at least 80%' but not the eTable 3 footnote's '>80%'.

rows.R: Table 1 p.5 (rendered): INQoL composite median (IQR) 84.0 (74.5-110.3) CLCN1 and 98.0 (56.0-120.0) SCN4A; footnote f gives a 0-100 scale (also Table 2 fn g, methods p.3). Upper quartiles exceed the scale maximum.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.3, p.5 Table 1, p.7-8 Table 2 (rendered 200 dpi).
rows.rationale: A quartile cannot exceed the maximum of a 0-100 scale; either the stated range or the summarized values are wrong (Table 2 baseline mean 96.89, SD 38.49, is also hard to reconcile with a 0-100 range). Baseline descriptive values only: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Table 1 p.5: 'Other' pretrial medication 7/16 (44) vs 5/11 (46), P = .62 (footnote: Mann-Whitney U). Recomputed: chi-square 0.93, Fisher 1.00, Mann-Whitney 0.93-0.95. Adjacent rows reproduce with Fisher (men 13/16 vs 7/11: 0.391, printed .39; mexiletine 2/16 vs 0/11: 0.499, printed .50). Also 5/11 = 45.5%, printed 46.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.5 Table 1 rendered at 200 dpi. R one-liner (chisq.test, fisher.test, wilcox.test).
rows.rationale: With nearly identical proportions (43.8% vs 45.5%) no standard test gives P = .62; the adjacent binary rows match Fisher exact tests (not the footnoted Mann-Whitney test). The printed P is probably wrong, although an unstated test cannot be fully excluded. Baseline comparison only: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 SCN4A fifth-attempt transient paresis: effect 13.71 (-1.96 to 25.47), P = .02. The CI includes 0 (CI-implied P about .05) and is asymmetric about 13.71; period changes -5.00 (placebo) and +9.56 (mexiletine) mean mexiletine worsened paresis, contradicting fn d ('all significant findings favored mexiletine'). Repeated in text p.6.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.4, p.6, p.7-8 Table 2 and footnotes (rendered 200 dpi). R back-calculation.
rows.rationale: Midpoint of the interval is 11.76, not 13.71; a symmetric t interval around 13.71 cannot be (-1.96, 25.47). The interval's implied P (about 0.05) conflicts with P = .02. The period columns give mexiletine - placebo = 9.56 - (-5.00) = 14.56 (worse with mexiletine, higher % = more severe), so if P = .02 is right this is a significant finding against mexiletine, contradicting footnote d. The estimate, interval and P cannot all be correct, and the subgroup result is cited in the text: confirmed, substantive.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 lower header: 'Treatment Effect (Placebo-Mexiletine)'. Lower-section effects equal mexiletine minus placebo changes: INQoL -21.44 - (-7.22) = -14.22 (printed -14.22); eyelid first -4.99 - (-0.74) = -4.25; TUG first -1.41 - (-0.15) = -1.26 (printed -1.25). Upper IVR section uses placebo minus mexiletine (5.55 - 2.42 = 3.13).
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.7-8 Table 2 and footnotes (rendered 200 dpi). Arithmetic from printed values.
rows.rationale: For most lower-section rows the printed effect equals the mexiletine-period change minus the placebo-period change, the opposite of the header. A reader applying the header would reverse the direction of every secondary effect (e.g., read INQoL -14.22 as mexiletine worse). Period columns allow reconstruction, but the header governs extraction of 27 effect estimates: substantive, direct.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 physical SF-36 placebo change 1.04 (-0.60 to 2.96): midpoint 1.18. Adjacent period intervals are symmetric about their means (mental placebo -1.85 (-4.81 to 1.11), mexiletine 8.66 (5.94 to 11.38)).
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.3, p.7 Table 2 (rendered 200 dpi). Arithmetic.
rows.rationale: A t-based interval for a mean change is symmetric; this one is off-centre by 0.14 points (about 9% of its half-width), which exceeds rounding. A transcription error in one limit or the mean is likely, but an asymmetric method cannot be excluded: probable_issue, minor_presentation (period change, not the treatment effect).

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 mental SF-36 effect 6.78 (1.64 to 11.92), P = .001. The interval implies t-test P = 0.012 (df 26) or z P = 0.010. Printed P is about 10 times too small; significance at .05 unchanged.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.3, p.4, p.7-8 Table 2. R back-calculation (se = width / (2 qt(.975, 26))).
rows.rationale: For a dependent t test the CI and P derive from the same mean and SE; 6.78 / 2.50 gives t = 2.71, P = 0.012. P = .001 is inconsistent with the interval. Conclusion (significant at .05, exploratory outcome) unchanged: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 first-attempt handgrip, placebo change 0.46 (-0.30 to -1.23) (minus sign visible in render): the upper limit is below the lower limit and the mean lies outside; likely 1.23. Treatment effect row reproduces (-2.39 - 0.46 = -2.85).
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.7 Table 2 rendered at 200 dpi; p.8 footnotes.
rows.rationale: An interval (-0.30, -1.23) is reversed and excludes its estimate; with +1.23 the interval is (-0.30, 1.23), midpoint 0.47, consistent with 0.46. Typographic sign error in a period-change cell: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7: several effects differ from mexiletine minus placebo period changes: SF-36 physical 7.62 vs 7.81; peak force first 26.73 vs 32.92, fifth 21.81 vs 24.08, mean 33.75 vs 37.23; transient paresis first -3.09 vs -3.7, fifth -9.29 vs -12.25, mean -6.30 vs -7.34; fifth handgrip CLCN1 -0.29 vs printed +0.04. Other rows reproduce to 0.01.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.3, p.4 (98% of secondary measures available), p.7-8 Table 2 (rendered 200 dpi). Arithmetic from printed values.
rows.rationale: For paired data the mean of differences equals the difference of means when the same observations contribute; this holds to rounding for eyelid, Timed Up&Go and most handgrip rows. The listed rows deviate by 10-30%, and the CLCN1 handgrip row reverses sign with an effect interval (-1.11 to 1.19) far wider than either period interval. With 98% of secondary measures collected, unpaired missing data are an unlikely full explanation, but per-outcome availability is not reported, so probable rather than confirmed. Effects are extractable values: substantive, direct.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 SCN4A fifth-attempt handgrip: -1.96 (-3.41 to 0.51), P = .009 (repeated p.8 text). CI includes 0 (CI-implied P about .05) and is asymmetric about -1.96 (midpoint -1.45). Period changes give mexiletine - placebo = -1.95, so the estimate fits the period data but not the interval or P.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.4, p.7 Table 2, p.8 text (rendered 200 dpi). R back-calculation.
rows.rationale: A t interval centred on -1.96 cannot be (-3.41, 0.51); the interval's implied P is about 0.05, not .009. The SCN4A subgroup result is used in the text to describe a genotype difference (interaction P = .04): confirmed, substantive.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 first eyelid -4.25 (-8.45 to -0.05), P = .05. CI-implied P = 0.0475 (t, df 26), which rounds to .05; a two-decimal P of .05 is compatible with an interval excluding 0. No inconsistency.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.4, p.7 Table 2. R back-calculation.
rows.rationale: The interval is symmetric about -4.25 and implies P = 0.047-0.048, consistent with the printed .05 after rounding to two decimals. A rounded P of .05 does not contradict P < .05. Explained by rounding: exclude.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 Timed Up&Go mean, placebo change 0.07 (-0.67 to 0.01): estimate above the upper limit; symmetric limit would be about 0.81. Treatment effect -1.12 = -1.05 - 0.07 reproduces.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.7 Table 2 (rendered 200 dpi), p.8 footnotes. Arithmetic.
rows.rationale: A mean cannot lie outside its own CI; with a symmetric interval the upper limit should be 0.07 + 0.74 = 0.81, suggesting a dropped digit. Period-change cell only: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Table 2 p.8 needle EMG grading: 0.67 (0.23 to 1.11), P < .001. Interval implies P = 0.004 (t, df 26) or 0.003 (z). Printed P too small; significance unchanged.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.3, p.4, p.8 Table 2 continuation (rendered 200 dpi). R back-calculation.
rows.rationale: SE = 0.88/(2 x 2.056) = 0.214, t = 3.13, P = 0.004. 'P < .001' is inconsistent with the interval. The finding remains significant at .05: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Protocol p.38 text: DSMB convenes if related serious adverse events reach >= 10% (three patients) or two or more of the same cardiac event. Figure 3 p.39 (rendered): 'cardiac events (AE/SAE) in more than 10% (three patients)' or two same cardiac events; a single cardiac event stops the individual trial.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf p.38 (text), p.39 Figure 3 rendered at 110 dpi and viewed.
rows.rationale: Text and figure differ in the event class (related SAEs of any type vs cardiac AEs/SAEs) and in the comparison (>= vs >10%, where 10% of 30 equals 3). The safety-review triggers are therefore ambiguous within the plan. No cardiac events occurred (report p.8) and one non-cardiac SAE occurred, so neither trigger was approached: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Protocol p.42 text: interim analyses use noninformative priors only. Figure 4 p.43 (rendered) shows '+ informative priors' entering at LR1 and LR2. Supp2 eMethods 1 (p.10) interim model uses vague priors, consistent with the text.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf p.41-43 (Figure 4 rendered at 110 dpi and viewed); joi180136supp2_prod.pdf p.10.
rows.rationale: The plan's text and its flowchart disagree on whether informative priors enter the interim stopping analyses. The text is explicit and gives a reason, and the reported interim code follows it, so the intended procedure is clear: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 baseline means: fifth handgrip total 1.36 vs genotype-weighted (16 x 0.93 + 11 x 2.59)/27 = 1.61; fifth transient paresis total 20.30 vs (16 x 24.35 + 11 x 9.12)/27 = 18.15 (mean row 24.11 vs 22.59). Stiffness reconciles (5.59 vs 5.65). Column C has no file/page; located via card.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.7 Table 2 and p.8 footnotes (rendered 200 dpi); final_report_1_6_2.md card C022 source table. Arithmetic.
rows.rationale: If the totals and genotype means come from the same patients, the totals must equal the 16/11-weighted average. They do not for these rows (implied CLCN1 weights 0.74 instead of 0.59). Different numbers of available baseline observations per genotype could explain it, but overall secondary-measure availability was 98%, which makes a weight shift of this size unlikely. Probable issue in baseline descriptors: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Protocol p.13 (5.1) difficult-airway characteristics: cervical immobility, obesity, large tongue, short neck, small mandible, facial or neck trauma, airway edema, blood in airway, vomit in airway. Report (p.1, p.2, Figure 1, Table 3): body fluids obscuring the view, airway obstruction or edema, obesity, short neck, small mandible, large tongue, facial trauma, c-spine immobilization.
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf p.13; joi180054supp2_prod.pdf p.7, p.9 (data form); jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.1, p.2, p.4 Figure 1, p.5 Table 1, p.7 Table 3 (rendered 170 dpi).
rows.rationale: The definition of the primary analysis population changed: neck trauma dropped (facial trauma only), airway obstruction added, and blood/vomit in airway generalized to body fluids obscuring the laryngeal view. Because the primary outcome is evaluated in this subgroup (380 patients), the population definition differs: substantive_difference.

rows.R: Protocol p.11 (4.1.1): randomization stratified by cervical collar, obesity or apparent facial/neck trauma vs none. Report p.3: strata were obesity or cervical immobilization vs neither (trauma criterion absent).
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf p.11; jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.2-3, p.7. Text layer.
rows.rationale: The stratification factor as reported omits facial/neck trauma. Either the stratification was implemented differently from the plan or it is misdescribed; in either case planned and reported randomization strata differ.

rows.R: Protocol p.9-10: hypoxemia recorded from start of the first attempt until 1 minute after ETT cuff inflation. Report p.3 and Table 3 fn b: during or within 1 minute after completion of the first intubation attempt (laryngoscope removal).
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf p.9-10; jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.1, p.3, p.7 Table 3 fn b, p.9 Table 5; joi180054supp2_prod.pdf p.2-3. Text layer.
rows.rationale: For a failed first attempt, the planned window extends through later attempts until the tube is placed, whereas the reported window ends 1 minute after the first attempt. With 7% of patients (more in the stylet group) needing further attempts, the outcome window differs materially for the patients most likely to desaturate.

rows.R: Protocol p.9-10: time to intubation from start of the attempt to inflation of the ETT cuff with the tube in the trachea. Report p.3, Table 3 fn c, eTable 1 fn: duration from laryngoscope insertion to removal.
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf p.9-10, p.19; jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.1, p.3-5, p.7 Table 3; joi180054supp2_prod.pdf p.2-3. Text layer.
rows.rationale: The endpoint changed from a time-to-successful-placement measure ending at cuff inflation to the duration of the first laryngoscopy, which also applies to failed attempts. Outcome definition differs.

rows.R: Protocol p.19 (8.2): enroll for 1 calendar year or 1000 patients, aiming for 374 difficult-airway patients. Report p.3: trial stopped when more than 374 difficult-airway patients were enrolled (380; 757 total, Sept 2016-Aug 2017).
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf p.19; jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.1, p.2-4 Figure 1, p.7. Text layer.
rows.rationale: The stated stopping criteria differ (time/total-enrollment cap in the protocol vs a difficult-airway count in the report). The trial ran about 12 months, so conduct may be consistent with either rule; whether the count-based rule was prespecified elsewhere cannot be determined from the supplied plan: indeterminate.

rows.R: Protocol p.19 (8.1): time-to-event data summarized by Kaplan-Meier 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles with 95% CIs and percentage censored. Report gives medians (IQR) with Hodges-Lehmann differences, KM curves, log-rank P and HR (p.5, Table 3, Figure 2, eTable 1); no KM percentiles with CIs or censoring percentages.
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf p.9, p.19; jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.1, p.4-5, p.7, p.8 Figure 2; joi180054supp2_prod.pdf p.2-4. Text layer.
rows.rationale: The planned descriptive KM summaries are not reported. Related outputs are given, so the difference is in presentation of summaries rather than in the inferential analysis; I leave L blank.

rows.R: Table 1 p.5 (rendered): saturation <90% and <80% use denominators 352 and 344, but footnote b says 19 and 24 patients lacked saturation (implying 362 and 352). 352 and 344 equal arm totals minus the patients missing heart rate (29 and 32).
rows.evidence: jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.5 Table 1 and footnote b (rendered 170 dpi); p.6 Table 2 (start-of-attempt denominators 360/343 reconcile with its footnote d). Arithmetic.
rows.rationale: 381 - 19 = 362 and 376 - 24 = 352, not 352 and 344; 381 - 29 = 352 and 376 - 32 = 344. Either the denominators or the footnote's ordering of missing counts is wrong. Baseline descriptor only: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Table 1 p.5 nested medical indications: altered mental status, cardiac arrest, septic shock and seizure percentages use the arm total (185/381 = 48.6%; 173/376 = 46.0%), while asthma/COPD and 'other' use the medical subtotal (16/318 = 5.0%, 44/318 = 13.8%; 23/315 = 7.3%, 41/315 = 13.0%). Denominator not stated.
rows.evidence: jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.5 Table 1 (rendered 170 dpi). Python recomputation of each cell with both denominators.
rows.rationale: Rows in the same nested block use different denominators without indication (e.g., 16/381 = 4.2% would print 4, but 5 is printed). Counts sum correctly (318 and 315). Percentages for baseline indications are inconsistent but the counts are clear: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Table 2 p.6: senior resident -5 (-10 to 0), P .03; junior 5 (0 to 10), P .03; screen during passage -6 (-12 to 0), P .04. Recomputed Wald CIs -10.27 to -0.46, 0.44 to 9.80, -12.47 to -0.43 (exclude 0); chi-square P 0.033, 0.033, 0.036. Integer rounding of limits explains the apparent conflict.
rows.evidence: jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.4 methods, p.6 Table 2 (rendered 170 dpi). R script (Wald and chi-square).
rows.rationale: The table rounds differences and limits to whole percentage points; limits of -0.46, 0.44 and -0.43 print as 0. The unrounded intervals exclude zero and agree with P < .05. No reporting error beyond coarse rounding: exclude.

rows.R: Table 3 p.7 (rendered) all-patient first-attempt duration: difference '1 (4 to -1)'; limits transposed. Supp2 eTable 1 p.2 (clustered analysis) prints 1 s (-1 s to 4 s).
rows.evidence: jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.4, p.7 Table 3 (rendered 170 dpi); joi180054supp2_prod.pdf p.2-3.
rows.rationale: Lower and upper limits are printed in descending order, unlike every other interval. The supplement shows the ascending form; the meaning is recoverable, but an extractor reading lower/upper by position would swap them: minor_presentation, possible downstream impact.

rows.R: Table 3 p.7 grade 4: 3/3 vs 2/5, difference 60 (17 to 100), P .09. Wald CI 17.1 to 102.9 (truncated at 100) and uncorrected chi-square P 0.090 both reproduce; Fisher P 0.20. Disagreement arises from applying Wald CI and chi-square to 8 patients, not from a reporting error.
rows.evidence: jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.4 methods, p.7 Table 3 (rendered 170 dpi). R (chisq.test, fisher.test, Wald).
rows.rationale: Both numbers are what the stated methods give; the Wald interval is unreliable with a 100% cell and n = 3, so the apparent CI/P conflict is a property of the methods in an 8-patient unplanned subgroup. The printed values are correctly computed, so I exclude, noting that neither statistic is informative here.

rows.R: Protocol p.8-9: primary outcome is first pass success; secondary 1 is first pass success without hypoxemia. Missing-data rule p.20-21 (8.6.1) for the primary outcome says video will be reviewed to determine whether 'first pass success without hypoxemia' was achieved.
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf p.8-9, p.20-21. Text layer.
rows.rationale: The primary-outcome missing-data procedure names the secondary composite as its recovery target. The intended target (first-pass success) is clear from the outcome definitions, and the report says no imputation was needed (missing data left as such): minor_presentation.

rows.R: Protocol p.20-21 (8.4.1, 8.6.2): interim analysis of the primary outcome, i.e., first pass success in difficult-airway patients. Supp2 eAppendix 1 p.6: interim used all 507 enrolled patients (250/257 vs 213/250) to decide continuation. Supplied protocol p.21 also leaves the interim sample size blank, whereas supp2 quotes '500'.
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf p.20-21; joi180054supp2_prod.pdf p.6; jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.3-4. Text layer.
rows.rationale: The plan defines the primary outcome in the difficult-airway subgroup and states the interim would analyze the primary outcome only; the reported interim used first-pass success in all patients. The analysis population for the futility decision differs. The quoted '500' does not appear in the supplied protocol text (blank).

rows.R: Protocol p.16 (lines 216-218) and supp2 eAppendix p.2: composite = total interventions performed among eligible patients / total possible interventions (pooled opportunities). Report p.3: composite 'calculated for each patient and then averaged'; Table 2 gives mean (SD) 88.2 (15.1) vs 84.8 (18.2). The GEE analysis (p.4) is opportunity-based.
rows.evidence: joi180070supp1_prod.pdf p.16, p.18-19; joi180070supp2_prod.pdf p.2; jama_wang_2018_oi_180070.pdf p.1, p.3-4, p.7 Table 2. Text layer.
rows.rationale: A pooled opportunity ratio weights patients by their number of eligible measures, whereas the per-patient average weights each patient equally; the two can differ. The reported descriptive composite uses the per-patient average while the planned definition (and the model) use pooled opportunities. The co-primary outcome definition differs between plan and report.

rows.R: Text p.4: 'A total of 4800 patients were enrolled ... and included in the primary analysis'; Table 2 uses 2400 per arm (all-or-none 1290/2400, 1147/2400). Figure 1 p.5 (rendered) labels 2003 and 1977 (12-month completers) as 'Patients included in primary analysis'.
rows.evidence: jama_wang_2018_oi_180070.pdf p.1, p.4, p.5 Figure 1 (rendered 170 dpi), p.7 Table 2. Arithmetic: 2400 - 397 = 2003; 2400 - 423 = 1977.
rows.rationale: The primary (in-hospital adherence) analysis used all 4800 patients, as stated in the text and shown by Table 2 denominators; the flow diagram instead labels the 12-month follow-up completers as the primary analysis population. The figure arithmetic itself is consistent. A labeling error in the flow diagram; the text and table make the intended population clear: minor_presentation, possible impact on extraction of analyzed n. Also, Figure 1 shows 3 hospitals that declined and were replaced, whereas the text says 3 hospitals had 'unexpected inability to conduct this trial'.

rows.R: Results p.5: outcomes 'at 3, 6, and 12 months after discharge'. Methods p.3, Table 3 fn b, Figure 2 axis (days after stroke symptom onset) and protocol p.16: after symptom onset. Median length of stay 12-13 days (Table 1).
rows.evidence: jama_wang_2018_oi_180070.pdf p.3, p.4, p.5, p.6 Table 1, p.8 Table 3 and Figure 2; joi180070supp1_prod.pdf p.16, p.19. Text layer.
rows.rationale: With a median stay of about 13 days, 'after discharge' and 'after symptom onset' differ by roughly 2 weeks, which matters for a 3-month window. However, the Methods, Table 3 footnote, Figure 2 axis and protocol all use symptom onset, so the single Results sentence is the outlier and the intended origin is clear: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Table 3 p.8 in-hospital death 11/2400 vs 23/2400: adjusted difference -0.7 (-1.1 to 0.2), P .009. Interval includes 0 and implies P about .035; it is also asymmetric about -0.7. The adjacent HR 0.96 (0.90-1.02) is implausibly precise for 34 deaths (crude ratio 0.48; SE(log) about 0.37).
rows.evidence: jama_wang_2018_oi_180070.pdf p.4 methods, p.5 narrative, p.8 Table 3. R back-calculation.
rows.rationale: P from the interval: SE = 1.3/3.92 = 0.33, z = 2.1, P = 0.035; an interval crossing zero cannot accompany P = .009 from the same model. The text says in-hospital mortality did not differ significantly, which agrees with the HR P = .14 and the interval but not with P = .009. The HR interval width (0.90-1.02) would need several thousand deaths, versus 11 + 23. At least one of the difference, interval, P or HR row is wrong; in-hospital death is a named secondary outcome: substantive, direct.

rows.R: Supp2 eTable 3 p.6: 3-month vascular death -1.43 (-2.33 to -0.54), P 0.001. Interval implies P = 0.0016-0.0019 allowing limit rounding; printed 0.001 is consistent with truncation. Other eTable 3 rows (e.g., 12-month -1.94 (-3.26 to -0.62), P .004) reproduce.
rows.evidence: joi180070supp2_prod.pdf p.6-7 eTable 3; jama_wang_2018_oi_180070.pdf p.4. R back-calculation.
rows.rationale: The interval excludes zero and the printed P is below .05, so the inferential readings agree; the residual difference (0.0018 vs 0.001) is within truncation of a three-decimal P value and has no consequence. Not a reportable inconsistency: exclude.

rows.R: Revised protocol p.63-64: intensive phase 90-min in-person sessions, telephone alternative 20 min; school-readiness program 45 min at each of 7 data collection points. Report p.2-3: weekly 90-minute sessions 'via either in-person groups or telephone calls'; control curriculum of six 30-minute activities.
rows.evidence: joi180075supp1_prod.pdf p.63-64 (text layer; digits present on these pages); jama_barkin_2018_oi_180075.pdf p.1-3.
rows.rationale: Two dose elements differ: telephone sessions (20 min planned vs 90 min reported) and the shared school-readiness sessions (7 x 45 min planned vs 6 x 30 min reported). These describe the intervention and control exposure; the report does not explain the change. Either the description or the delivery differs from the plan.

rows.R: Original protocol p.16: child triceps skinfold and waist circumference listed with BMI under primary outcomes (Table 2); parental BMI, skinfold and waist as secondary (Table 3). Revised p.67 lists 7 secondary outcomes without them. Report p.3 states parent anthropometrics and child waist/triceps were collected but not included as secondary outcomes (disclosed).
rows.evidence: joi180075supp1_prod.pdf p.16, p.45, p.67 (page 67 text layer partly garbled; content read in context), p.98; jama_barkin_2018_oi_180075.pdf p.1, p.3, p.8 Table 2.
rows.rationale: Outcomes that the original protocol named as primary (child adiposity measures) or secondary (parent anthropometrics) are not analyzed in the report, which agrees with the revised protocol and discloses the omission. Under the review rule, a disclosed change in outcome status is retained as a difference.

rows.R: Original p.40-42, revised p.93-95 and final summary p.113 ('we still plan to do this'): sensitivity analyses of the primary BMI model (constrained multiple imputation, MI with auxiliary variables, spline age terms, cluster-structure SEs, baseline BMI x treatment). Report p.4-7 and supp2 give ML mixed-model results and moderator analyses only; no sensitivity results.
rows.evidence: joi180075supp1_prod.pdf p.40-42, p.93-95, p.113 (p.40 bottom rendered to recover digits missing from text layer); jama_barkin_2018_oi_180075.pdf p.4, p.6-7; joi180075supp2_prod.pdf (all pages searched).
rows.rationale: The final plan explicitly retains missing-data and model-specification sensitivity analyses for the primary outcome; none is reported. Planned primary-outcome sensitivity analyses absent: substantive_difference.

rows.R: Report p.4: secondary and post hoc outcomes analyzed by OLS and robust Poisson regression; 'Models were prespecified'. Supplied original, revised and final plans (searched for Poisson, least squares, secondary model specifications) contain no such models for the secondary outcomes or obesity.
rows.evidence: joi180075supp1_prod.pdf p.45-48, p.67, p.98-101, p.113 (text search for 'poisson', 'least squares', 'logistic'); jama_barkin_2018_oi_180075.pdf p.4, p.8 Table 2 fn f, p.9 Table 3 fn b.
rows.rationale: An analysis described as prespecified has no specification in the supplied plans. The prespecification may be documented elsewhere, but within the supplied material the claim has no plan basis. Recorded as a planned-versus-reported difference.

rows.R: Table 3 p.9 obesity at 3 months: RR 0.51 (0.29-0.92), P .02, Benjamini-Hochberg corrected P .10. BH over the 5 time points reproduces all corrected P values (.02 x 5 = .10; .13 x 5/2 and .16 x 5/3 give .27). An unadjusted CI excluding 1 with a nonsignificant FDR-adjusted P is expected; the text states 'before correcting for multiple comparisons'.
rows.evidence: jama_barkin_2018_oi_180075.pdf p.4 methods, p.7 Post-Hoc Analyses, p.9 Table 3 and footnotes. Arithmetic BH recomputation.
rows.rationale: The CI is not multiplicity-adjusted, whereas the corrected P is; the table labels both. The corrected P values are computed correctly. No inconsistency.

rows.R: Original plan p.36 (rendered; digits absent from text layer): '600 dyads per cohort (300 per region/site), and a total sample size of 600'. Same plan p.13 and p.40 (rendered): three cohorts of 200 dyads, retention to 160 per cohort and 480 total.
rows.evidence: joi180075supp1_prod.pdf p.13, p.36-37, p.40 (p.36 and p.40 rendered at 150 dpi because the text layer omits numerals), p.94.
rows.rationale: '600 dyads per cohort' conflicts with three cohorts of 200; 600 is the trial total, which the same sentence also gives, and the retention arithmetic (3 x 160 = 480) uses 200 per cohort. The intended design (600 total, 200 per cohort) is clear from context: minor_presentation.

rows.R: Supp2 eTable 1 p.2: 3-month adjusted BMI difference -0.01 (-0.12, 0.13), P 0.83. Interval midpoint is +0.005; other rows are centred on their estimates (e.g., -0.04 (-0.20, 0.12)). With +0.01 (unrounded about 0.014) the P of 0.83 also fits. Sign error likely.
rows.evidence: joi180075supp2_prod.pdf p.2 eTable 1. Arithmetic: SE = 0.25/3.92 = 0.064; estimate 0.014 gives P = 0.83.
rows.rationale: A model-based Wald interval is symmetric about its estimate; -0.01 lies outside the central half of (-0.12, 0.13) and the P value matches a small positive estimate. Observed means at 3 months are 16.7 vs 16.6 (intervention higher). The estimate is near zero either way and the primary trajectory test is unaffected: minor_presentation.
